In mathematics, the '''Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski measurable selection theorem''' is a result from [[measure theory]] that gives a sufficient condition for a [[set-valued function]] to have a measurable [[selection function]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Aliprantis|last2=Border|title=Infinite-dimensional analysis. A hitchhiker's guide.|date=2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|first=Alexander S.|last=Kechris|title=Classical descriptive set theory|url=https://archive.org/details/classicaldescrip0000kech|url-access=registration|publisher=Springer-Verlag|date=1995|isbn=9780387943749 }} Theorem (12.13) on page 76.</ref><ref>{{cite book|first=S.M.|last=Srivastava|title=A course on Borel sets|url=https://archive.org/details/springer_10.1007-978-0-387-22767-2|publisher=Springer-Verlag|date=1998|isbn=9780387984124 }} Sect. 5.2 "Kuratowski and Ryll-Nardzewski’s theorem".</ref>  It is named after the Polish mathematicians [[Kazimierz Kuratowski]] and [[Czesław Ryll-Nardzewski]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kuratowski|first1=K.|last2=Ryll-Nardzewski|first2=C.|title=A general theorem on selectors|journal=Bull. Acad. Polon. Sci. Sér. Sci. Math. Astronom. Phys.|volume=13|year=1965|pages=397–403}}</ref>

Many classical selection results follow from this theorem<ref>{{Citation|last = Graf| first  = Siegfried|contribution = Selected results on measurable selections|year   = 1982|title  = Proceedings of the 10th Winter School on Abstract Analysis|publisher = Circolo Matematico di Palermo |contribution-url = http://dml.cz/dmlcz/701265 }}</ref> and it is widely used in [[mathematical economics]] and [[optimal control]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cascales |first1=Bernardo |last2=Kadets |first2=Vladimir |last3=Rodríguez |first3=José |date=2010 |title=Measurability and Selections of Multi-Functions in Banach Spaces
 |url=http://www.um.es/beca/papers/MeasSelections.pdf |journal=Journal of Convex Analysis |volume=17 |issue=1 |pages=229–240 |access-date=28 June 2018}}</ref>

== Statement of the theorem == 
Let <math> X </math> be a [[Polish space]], <math> \mathcal{B} (X) </math> the [[Borel set|Borel]] [[sigma-algebra|&sigma;-algebra]] of <math> X </math>,  <math> (\Omega, \mathcal{F}) </math> a [[measurable space]] and <math> \psi </math> a multifunction on <math> \Omega</math> taking values in the set of nonempty closed subsets of <math> X </math>.  

Suppose that <math> \psi </math> is <math> \mathcal{F} </math>-weakly measurable, that is, for every open subset <math> U </math> of <math> X </math>, we have

:<math>\{\omega : \psi (\omega) \cap U \neq \empty \} \in \mathcal{F}. </math>

Then <math> \psi </math> has a [[Choice function|selection]] that is <math> \mathcal{F} </math>-<math> \mathcal{B} (X) </math>-measurable.<ref>V. I. Bogachev, [https://www.springer.com/math/analysis/book/978-3-540-34513-8 "Measure Theory"] Volume II, page 36.</ref>
